written: 2026-10-27 04:30 CDT, before any Phase 2 training run and before any Phase 2 dev episode
question: Does a lamp/target auxiliary loss (with clean DAgger labels) make the learned policy tie 'done' to the lamp in set_lamp?
step_1_result: results/p2/lamp_probe.json: a small CNN reads the bot-labelled lamp state from fresh-sighting frames at 64x64 with 0.953 accuracy on train configs 200-299 (32x32: 0.906). The frame size is not the bottleneck, so the frame stays 64x64 and the change is the auxiliary loss.
data: Train split only: the 888 M4 demos (results/m5/bc_index.jsonl) + DAgger round 1 and round 2 episodes (episodes/dagger_index.jsonl, dagger2_index.jsonl), each truncated at its first cmd_bot done tick (inclusive), which is what the fixed recorder would have stored.
aux_labels: From the bot's own beliefs, never from simulator truth: lamp (unknown/on/off) = memory lamp sighting newer than the bot's latest own press event; match (unknown/matches target/mismatch), set_lamp episodes only.

runs.P2-B: 64x64, aux weight 1.0, done head also reads the match-head probabilities
runs.common: from scratch, seed 0, 16,000 steps, batch 32, window 128 / burn-in 32 / p_start 0.2, lr 3e-4, checkpoints every 4,000 steps, through bin/gpu_run with --max-minutes 45, one training at a time

dev_sets.diagnostic_demos: Reference-bot set_lamp episodes recorded on instances-dev 0010-0029, arrangements-dev 0000-0019, appearances-dev 0000-0019, distractor-dev 0000-0019 (k=0): 80 episodes, never trained on.
dev_sets.closed_loop: set_lamp, policy driving, on instances/arrangements/appearances/distractor-dev 0000-0009 (k=0): 40 episodes; plus the M5 selection set (instances-dev 0000-0009 x 3 tasks) to check go-and-return and find-ball.

metrics.open_loop_lamp_auc: Teacher-forced on the diagnostic demos: the policy's done logit at the bot's first lamp_check tick; AUC of no-press episodes (the bot says done there) vs press-needed episodes (the bot goes to press). M5's DAgger policy is measured the same way as the baseline.
metrics.open_loop_early_done: press-needed diagnostic demos where the done logit exceeds 0 anywhere in the 30 ticks up to the lamp_check tick
metrics.aux_accuracy: match-head and lamp-head accuracy on known-belief ticks of the diagnostic demos
metrics.closed_loop: press-needed successes, no-press successes, presses made, 'said done without pressing' in press-needed episodes, falls

selection_rule: Within each run, every checkpoint is run closed loop on the 40 set_lamp dev episodes. Pick: most press-needed successes, then higher open-loop lamp AUC, then most no-press successes, then the earlier step. Loss is not used.
pass_criteria: The policy 'ties done to the lamp' if (1) open-loop lamp AUC >= 0.9 and (2) in closed loop it says done without pressing in at most half of the press-needed dev episodes and succeeds in at least one press-needed episode. Reported either way; the reserved test sets are not used in Phase 2 for this question.
not_changed: No test-set episode is run for this question. The bot, judges, interface and splits stay frozen.

amendments.finding: P2-A (as specified) failed the dev check at every checkpoint (lamp AUC 0.41-0.49, 0/18 press-needed; results/p2/select_p2_a.json, diag files kept). Cause: its image encoder died. The last conv layer had 0% of channels positive for any frame by step 4,000, so image features were constant and the policy was blind. Short runs show plain-ReLU training kills that layer within ~250 steps on some seeds in both trainers (p2_train and M5's m5_train); M5's runs happened to survive. The earlier 96x96 probe failure (0.606/0.506) looks like the same thing.
amendments.change: The image encoder uses leaky ReLU (slope 0.05; Policy2 act='leaky'), and training logs c4_alive every 500 steps. Runs become P2-A' (64, aux 1, leaky), P2-B' (+ done reads match), P2-C' (aux 0, leaky), same seed 0 and settings, one at a time. P2-A is reported as a negative result.
amendments.extra_checks: Per checkpoint: lamp-head accuracy split by in-view (fresh sighting) vs remembered ticks on dev demos, and a linear lamp probe on the frozen image features (train configs 0-199 / 200-299). If in-view accuracy stays below ~85% by the last checkpoint, the next lever is masking the aux loss to ticks whose sighting lies inside the window, then encoder pretraining on the bot's per-frame detections.

arms.bot_alone: reference bot drives from tick 0, budget 900 (baseline).

check_A_teacher_takeover.metrics: Per arm, split press-needed / no-press: success; bot said done with the simulator lamp wrong; presses; falls; episodes the policy ended (said done) before T (reported, removed from that arm's denominator).
check_A_teacher_takeover.gate: The shadow bot is a valid recovery teacher if, at T=250, its press-needed success after takeover is at least 80% of bot_alone's press-needed success, and it says done with the lamp wrong in at most 5% of its finishes. If the shadow bot fails but fresh_250 passes, the recovery round restarts the bot at each takeover. If both fail, recovery demonstrations need a different teacher (e.g. the oracle's geometry for the approach) and the round is re-planned.

check_B_teacher_forced_turn.data: The 80 dev bot demos (episodes/p2_dev), teacher-forced as in p2_vx_check; policies P2-A' (s0, s1), P2-D, P2-E at their picked checkpoints.
check_B_teacher_forced_turn.metrics: On the bot's turn-in-place ticks (|wz| > 0.1, vx == 0): share of policy wz with the bot's sign, mean |wz|, share with |wz| >= 0.5 (starts a turn on this body). The same on turning-while-walking ticks (sign and mean |wz| only). Also, replay-only diagnostic on the DAgger round 3 episodes: on ticks where P2-A' commanded a turn in place, the share where the duck's yaw actually changed (truth yaw, analysis only; never a label or input).
check_B_teacher_forced_turn.decision: If on the bot's turn-in-place ticks the policy has the bot's sign on >= 90% and |wz| >= 0.5 on >= 70%, the turn output is fine in the bot's states and the closed-loop weakness is a state-distribution problem (recovery data is the fix). Otherwise the turn output itself is too weak or unsure: the recovery round adds a discrete turn head (left / none / right, decoded to +-0.55 / 0 in place), trained and compared alongside.

amendments.decision: Success first. An arm is 'promising' if on the confirmation rooms (a) each seed's press-needed successes exceed R3's seed mean, and (b) the arm's two-seed sum beats R3's sum by at least 3; no-press successes reported per seed, and an arm whose two-seed no-press sum is more than 4 below R3's is flagged as trading no-press for press. These are operational pilot thresholds, not statistical tests. Done-after-press is reported split by lamp right / wrong at the done, not used as a bar. H vs Hr isolates carried memory; E vs R3 isolates ending exposure. Not promising -> don't scale it; skill selection (Astra option 2) stays the next capability experiment.

amendments.written_before: any H/Hr training step under these settings (the first H s0 / Hr s0 attempts were stopped at ~2,000 steps and set aside as runs/failed_p2_{h,hr}_s0_1749; no checkpoint, no dev episode)
amendments.finding: Stream training from scratch does not learn on the real data: H s0 and Hr s0 stayed flat for 2,000 steps (loss ~4.1-4.3, turn CE ~1.0 near chance; E s0 and R3 s0 learned by step 300-1,000). Bounded scratch experiments (batch 32, 300-800 steps, scratchpad dbg_stream.py) located it: the window sampler with p_start 0 (no window starting at an episode's first tick) also fails; chunk sampling (tick-weighted, aligned 128-tick chunks, zero memory) fails with or without a 32-tick burn-in mask, without the done positives, without the last partial chunk, and with or without an explicit zero initial state; a 512-stream pool (to remove correlation between consecutive batches) also fails; i.i.d. chunks with uniform episode choice (more first chunks) learn. Learning onset depends on episode-start windows; the exact mechanism is not established. After a 400-step windowed warm-up, pooled stream training keeps learning (cross-evaluated on fixed window batches: 2.40 vs 2.29 for 800 window steps).
amendments.change: H and Hr: the first 2,000 steps use the R3 window sampler (identical to R3's first 2,000 steps' sampling scheme), then stream training with a pool of 512 streams in progress, 32 drawn at random per step, each advancing one 128-tick chunk with its own carried memory (H) or zero memory (Hr). A drawn stream's memory was computed under the weights of its previous draw (~16 steps earlier on average). p2_train defaults: --stream-pool 512, --stream-warmup 2000.
amendments.consequence: H vs Hr still isolates carried memory (same warm-up, same chunks). H/Hr vs R3 now differ only after step 2,000. Everything else in amendment 7 unchanged.
